findings.title: Uninitialized Stack Elements
findings.trigger: Pushing an element to an uninitialized stack slot
findings.assumptions: The type T might not have a default constructor, and pushing to an uninitialized slot could lead to undefined behavior.

findings.title: Out-of-Bounds Write
findings.trigger: Pushing more elements than the stack size allows
findings.assumptions: The stack size is not validated against the maximum limit, and pushing beyond the allocated size could lead to a buffer overflow.

findings.title: Use After Free
findings.trigger: Popping from an empty stack and then accessing the stack array
findings.assumptions: The destructor does not set the arr pointer to nullptr, and accessing the array after deletion could lead to a use-after-free error.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: Returning an instance of T that could be used to construct an OS command
findings.assumptions: If T is a string-like type and the emptyValue instance contains shell metacharacters, it could be used to inject a command.
